title: A phospholipid
caption: Glycerol carries two fatty acid tails (non-polar, hydrophobic) and a phosphate head with choline (charged, hydrophilic). Having both parts makes the molecule amphipathic, which is why phospholipids assemble into a bilayer in water.
alt: Structure of a phosphatidylcholine with a saturated palmitic acid tail, an unsaturated oleic acid tail with a cis double bond, and a phosphate and choline head.
description: Two fatty acid tails joined to glycerol by ester bonds: one saturated, one with a cis double bond.
A phosphate group on the third carbon of glycerol, linked to choline: the polar head.
Tails: hydrophobic. Head: hydrophilic. The molecule is amphipathic.
